analysis: All changed files in this batch are Swift test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. No production source, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or authorization code is changed. The tests assert that Flint is paged-only. ModelBenchmarkDispatchTests.swift lines 19-31 expect Flint to use the native benchmark route and to skip scalar prefill in ThroughputSweep. FlintContextAdmissionTests.swift lines 152-179 expect that a per-model contiguous override makes the production slot build fail with pagedUnavailable. The same file's makeBridge now passes "paged" (line 208). FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests.swift lines 58-125 expect the crash-loop guard, kill switch, explicit contiguous selection, bad paged dtype and failed preflight to refuse Flint instead of silently falling back to contiguous. FlintPolicyTests.swift lines 130-143 expect the global balanced default never to block Flint, while per-model and environment quantization overrides still raise flintRequiresNative. The tests use /dev/null for the KV guard path, temp files that are cleaned up, and a router-mode test with no listener, so they open no new attack surface. Because this batch contains only tests, it cannot show that the production behavior they assert (the EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend refusal paths, ModelBenchmark and ThroughputSweep dispatch, EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy) is actually implemented. The corresponding production-source changes need review elsewhere. T-041 (prefix cache) is not affected by this batch: tests set PrefixCachePolicy.environmentFlag to "0", and no cache storage, TTL, or HMAC behavior is touched. No threat-model regression was identified in the supplied evidence.
